requirement: Implement EPIC-2 story 2.4: a minimal source and clip UI that processes audio through the localhost sidecar and loads the returned draft into the editor.

architecture.decision: Add a small typed reduction client and a focused SourcePanel component above the grid; App remains the editor-state owner and adopts a validated draft through its existing lesson loader.
alternatives: Put fetch and form state directly in App.tsx
tradeoffs: One client module and one component keep the network trust boundary testable and avoid bloating App or conflating source creation with saved lessons.

tasks.title: Create the reduction client boundary
tasks.intent: Build multipart requests, surface sidecar errors, enrich draft identity/title, and validate before editor adoption.
constraints: Accept exactly one file or URL
Do not mutate editor state on invalid responses
tasks.acceptance: A typed client posts source/clip/BPM fields to localhost, converts a valid draft into a Lesson with id/title, and throws actionable errors for HTTP or schema failures.
tasks.result: Added a typed multipart reduction client with local validation, actionable HTTP errors, UUID/title enrichment, and the existing Lesson validator as the response trust boundary.

tasks.title: Build and integrate the source panel
tasks.intent: Add accessible file/YouTube, clip, optional BPM, Process, busy, success, and error states in the locked stealth design.
constraints: Keep fetch in the event handler
tasks.acceptance: The user can choose file or YouTube, enter a <=15s range and optional BPM, Process once, see honest progress/errors, and receive the draft in the existing editor ready to save.
tasks.visual: Inspect desktop and <=820px layouts, focus states, status semantics, and the 32-tick clip rail.
tasks.result: Added and integrated an accessible stealth source panel with file/YouTube modes, clip/BPM controls, a 32-tick rail, honest busy/error/success states, and draft adoption through the existing editor loader.
evidence: React best-practices review passed hooks, a11y, render, and TypeScript checks
